text: 🍿 The Mummy 4 is filming. Fraser and Weisz are back. 📆 Estreno: October 15, 2027 🎭 Género: #Action #Adventure ✈️ Add to watchlist Brendan Fraser and Rachel Weisz back for a direct sequel to The Mummy Returns , with Radio Silence ( Ready or Not ) directing. Horror directors on a legacy adventure franchise. I buy that. Imhotep back. Beni back. Yes, both of them. After the third film buried this franchise alive, zero apologies is the right approach. 🏜️

🎬 Zach Cregger has thoughts on Hollywood's viral horror gold rush. Good ones. Cregger is out here saying what few working directors will say out loud: chasing a hot IP without loving the story is a fast track to a bad movie. He knows because he lived it, with the 2009 comedy Miss March. Coming from the guy who turned Barbarian into one of the sharpest horror films of the decade, that carries weight. He's also not writing the Weapons spin-off Gladys himself. Zach Shields has that one. Smart move: you don't have to direct everything in your orbit just because your name is on it. Restraint is underrated in this industry.

🍿 Pattinson plays Chris Hansen. Hansen is not pleased. This is already fascinating. 📆 Estreno: September 25, 2026 🎭 Género: #Thriller #CrimeDrama ✈️ Add to watchlist Director Lance Oppenheim, who apparently first encountered "To Catch a Predator" through South Park parodies, has turned that secondhand mythology into an A24 thriller. That detail matters, because Primetime feels less like a biopic and more like an obsession with why Hansen became an icon in the first place. Pattinson nailed it when he said there's "something he's doing" behind that show's staying power, something you can't name even after watching thousands of hours. The camera loves certain people for reasons that defy logic. Hansen is one of them. Hansen walking out of the A24 screening over an NDA is, weirdly, very on-brand.
